parameters.content:
# 07 - Task Test Harness

**What this workflow does**
A manually triggered harness that sits outside the lead path: nothing calls it and nothing in the pipeline depends on it. It POSTs booth scans to workflow 01's live production webhook exactly as a badge scanner would, waits for the async tail, then scores each scan against stored state and returns one PASS/FAIL row per scan - so a claim about the pipeline can be checked instead of trusted.

## The assumptions it rests on

1. **A demo that needs a second tool is a demo that breaks.** No Postman, no curl, no editing code to change a test.
2. **The webhook reply is not the answer.** Workflow 01 answers the scanner in about two seconds and keeps working for another minute. Scoring therefore reads the stored decision from `oak_deliveries`, never the HTTP reply - and reports `changed_after_the_202` when the two disagree.
3. **A soft failure nobody asserts on is indistinguishable from success.** Slack delivery is a scored check, not a hope. A channel the app has not joined fails the run instead of quietly posting nowhere.
4. **Tests belong in data, not in code.** Cases live in the `oak_test_payloads` table, so adding one is a row, not an edit.

## How to run it

Hit **Execute workflow**. With `Paste JSON Here` left at `"scans": []`, the **enabled** rows of `oak_test_payloads` run - the four task leads. To run more without toggling rows one by one, set the n8n variable `OAK_TEST_SUITE`: `all` runs every row, a suite name runs that suite whatever its `enabled` flag, and a name no row carries fails the run instead of falling back to the four. Put one or more scan objects in `scans` for a one-off; anything there takes precedence over the table and the variable.

A scan object reaches the webhook as the task payload **verbatim**: the harness deletes the test-only `expect` key before the POST. Expectations otherwise come from the table, matched by `scan_id`, and an inline `expect` overrides that lookup. Only `reset`, `gap_seconds` and `settle_seconds` are harness controls, and they sit outside `scans`.

## What the reset does

Deletes only rows tagged `oak-live-event-2026`, so the same `scan_id` can be replayed past the duplicate guard and every visitor looks new again. Real event data with any other `event_id` is untouched. `reset: false` is what turns a second scan of the same badge into a returning visitor.

## What comes back

One row per lead: what the webhook answered versus what was finally stored, tier, persona, score, the rule that fired, the Slack channel and whether Slack accepted the message, the HubSpot contact id, the resolved headcount with its source and confidence, and whether enrichment was reused from cache.

**Expected for the task suite:** Rachel → `tier_1` / `#booth-hot` · Hiroshi → `matched` / `#booth-matched` · David → `out_of_scope` / `#booth-out-of-scope` · Sarah → `competitor_intel` / `#competitive-intel`

## What a PASS asserts

Matching the classification is the last check, not the only one. An accepted scan has to be accepted by the webhook, leave an `oak_deliveries` row, reach `status: complete` inside the settle wait, and - when the stored decision names a channel - have Slack confirm the message, before `classification`, `persona` and `channel` are compared at all. The ledger check is what separates a pipeline still running from one that died after the `202`.

A case whose expectation is `{"accepted": false}` inverts the first two: the webhook must reject it and no `oak_deliveries` row may exist. That is the only way a case passes by nothing happening, and it is how the invalid-scan row in the table is scored.

## Where it can fail

Two scans in one run sharing a `scan_id` is a deliberate hard error - the duplicate guard would drop the second one silently, and a test that silently halves itself is worse than no test. Beyond that, the harness is honest by construction: it scores from stored state, so anything it reports green actually happened.

nodes.name: Paste JSON Here
nodes.notes: One-off runs. Put one or more scan objects in scans and hit Execute workflow. Leave scans empty to use the enabled rows in oak_test_payloads instead. An optional expect on any scan gives PASS/FAIL.

nodes.name: Build Test Plan
nodes.notes: Turns table rows, or pasted scans, into one plan item per scan with its expectation looked up by scan_id. The OAK_TEST_SUITE variable picks the rows: unset runs the enabled ones, all runs every row, any other value runs that suite and fails if no row has it; the four payloads in code are only a fallback when no row is enabled. OAK_BOOTH_WEBHOOK_URL sets the webhook target and defaults to this instance when unset.

nodes.name: Load Test Payloads
nodes.notes: Loads every row that has a payload_json, not only the enabled ones: the rows OAK_TEST_SUITE selects (the enabled ones by default) supply the scans, all rows supply expectations by scan_id. Add, edit or toggle tests in the n8n Data Tables UI; nothing here needs a code change.
